description:
Move Chase-Pyndiah reliability ordering and hard decisions onto canonical soft-value helpers while preserving SISO behavior.

## Background

The Chase-Pyndiah engine accepts raw `f32` soft values, owns a private magnitude sorter, and duplicates the sign-to-bit rule. The canonical magnitude primitive serves this consumer without forcing an `Llr` representation.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Obtains ascending reliability indices from the canonical `f32` magnitude permutation.
- [hard] REQ-02: Obtains hard decisions from the canonical sign convention while preserving zero-to-bit-zero behavior.
- [hard] REQ-03: Preserves candidate selection, correction, and SISO output on existing product-code fixtures.
- [hard] REQ-04: Covers tied magnitudes, signed zero, and infinite magnitudes without a private reliability comparator or sign test.
title: Chase-Pyndiah reliability migration
